title: Graph: consumer surplus, Grab as monopoly vs competition
scenario: Grab faces P = 339 − Q (rides per minute) with MC = 147 THB. The monopoly equilibrium is Q = 96 at P = 243; the competitive equilibrium is Q = 192 at P = 147. Areas A, B, C and D are marked on the graph.

questions.stem: Which area is consumer surplus in the competitive (Bertrand) equilibrium?
questions.explanation: At P = 147 consumers get everything under demand and above 147: A + B + C = ½ × 192 × 192 = 18,432.

questions.stem: Which area is consumer surplus in the monopoly equilibrium?
questions.explanation: At P = 243 consumers keep only the triangle above 243: A = ½ × 96 × 96 = 4,608.

questions.stem: Moving from competition to monopoly, what happens to area C?
choices: It goes from consumers to the monopolist
questions.explanation: C is the rectangle between 147 and 243 over the first 96 rides: consumer surplus under competition, producer surplus (profit) under monopoly.

questions.stem: Which area is the deadweight loss of monopoly?
questions.explanation: B is the triangle between demand and MC from 96 to 192 rides: trades that would happen under competition but do not under monopoly. Nobody gets it.

questions.stem: What is the value of area C?
Why does the MR line reach the horizontal axis at 169.5?
choices: It is half the competitive output
questions.explanation: MR falls twice as fast as demand, so it hits zero at half of 339. Competitive output is 192; demand reaches zero at 339.
